To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the asymptotic performance (in terms of output SINR) of a blind receiver is independent of the SNR of the desired user; and (ii) the asymptotic BER of a blind or group-blind receiver is related to its output SINR simply through Q(x) = 1/sqrt(2 pi) int_{x}^{infty} e^{-t^2/2} dt.
the capacity of blind or group-blind receivers is not only limited by the interference, but also limited by the estimation error, and the BER is a simple function of the SINR.

the asymptotic performance analysis of the blind and groupblind linear MMSE multiuser receivers can be characterized by three asymptotic quantities: the asymptotic average SINR, the asymptotic average residual interference, and the asymptotic average estimation error.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the large-system performance of blind and groupblind receivers, which is a fundamental problem in the design and analysis of wireless communications systems.
a large-system performance characterization of blind and group blind multiuser receivers.
the asymptotic performance analysis of blind or group-blind linear multiuser receivers in a large system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the asymptotic BER of a wireless system using blind or group-blind linear MMSE receivers is given by a Q function of a linear function of the SINR.

the asymptotic performance analysis for blind and group-blind linear MMSE receivers is similar to that of exact linear MMSE receivers in terms of the asymptotic SINR, but different in terms of the residual interference distribution.
the performance of blind and groupblind multiuser receivers is characterized by three factors: the SNR, the interference level, and the estimation error.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the large-system analysis provides a powerful tool for analyzing the asymptotic performance and the BER of blind or group-blind linear receivers.
in a large-system regime with binary spreading, the performance of blind and groupblind receivers are characterized by their SINR and residual interference.

the performance of a blind or group-blind receiver is determined by the SINR and the residual interference, and the residual interference is independent of the spreading sequences, but depends on the estimation method.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, for blind and group-blind detection, the performance of a large-scale system is determined by the asymptotic output SINR and the residual interference, both of which are independent of the spreading sequences and hence can be characterized by simple closed-form expressions.
the performance of a blind or group-blind receiver in a large system is determined by the asymptotic output SINR.

, while the blind or group-blind linear MMSE receivers are not optimal in a small system, they can achieve a performance that is within 3 dB of the optimal performance when the system is sufficiently large, provided that the SNR of the desired user is sufficiently large.
